decisions.reason: The indoor air quality sensor module is tightly tied to the firm's established sensing, electronics, firmware, and API capabilities, so it remains a product the firm can continue to learn from and refine efficiently.
As a successor to an earlier voltage-measurement module, it rests on very strong prior knowledge and proven customer use cases, making discontinuation unlikely.

The MQTT proxy still fits the firm's connectivity and software-binding strengths, but as a software-side complement with less hardware lock-in it remains somewhat easier to remove if usage is limited.
The carbon dioxide sensor module sits squarely within the firm's core sensing platform, where existing electronics, firmware, and documentation capabilities support continued commercial improvement.

The touch panel accessory is more peripheral to the firm's main knowledge base than its sensing and interface modules, so its weaker absorptive fit makes it the most likely candidate for resource reallocation to core platform development.
